title: HOG Features
oneLine: Describe shape by the histogram of gradient orientations in each cell.

paras: Before deep nets, HOG was the go-to descriptor for object shape, especially pedestrians. Split the image into small cells, build a histogram of gradient orientations in each, then normalize over blocks for lighting invariance. The result is a compact vector capturing local edge structure.
Each pixel votes into orientation bins weighted by gradient magnitude:
sections.texNote: Block normalization across neighboring cells gives robustness to illumination.

sections.code:
import numpy as np
mag = np.hypot(Gx, Gy)
ori = (np.degrees(np.arctan2(Gy, Gx)) % 180)
bins = (ori / 20).astype(int)            # 9 orientation bins per cell
# accumulate mag into per-cell histograms, then block-normalize
sections.caption: Orientation histograms per cell, normalized per block.

takeaways: HOG encodes shape as per-cell gradient-orientation histograms.
It powered classical detection before CNNs.
